questions.question:
Two Statements are given followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All sparrows are birds.

Some owls are birds.

**Conclusions:**

I. No sparrow is an owl.

II. Some sparrows are owls.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Either conclusion I or II follows.

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2a2b222b541484358e565f6fc0eb6cb4a10eb806dcabc4e39e88ab43aa46e01b.png] 

Conclusions:

I. No sparrow is an owl → Does not Follow (As, all sparrows are birds and some owls are birds. So, as no direct negative or cross relation is given between sparrow and owls therefore, it is definitely false)

II. Some sparrows are owls → Does not Follow (As, all sparrows are birds and some owls are birds. So, it is possible but not definitely true)

∴ Here,

 
• Elements i.e sparrow and owl are same in both the conclusions.
 
• Both the conclusions are individually does not follow(possible but not definitely true).
 
• Conclusion I and II are complementary pair i.e Some and No

Hence, the correct answer is "Either conclusion I or II follows".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

Conditions of either or case

 
• The elements should be same in both the conclusions
 
• Both conclusions should possible but not definitely true.
 
• One of the conclusion should be negative and one of the conclusion should be positive i.e complimentary pair.
 
• Complimentary pairs :

 
• ​some + no and all + some not
 
• Some + Some not and All + no are not Complimentary pair.

questions.question:
Study the given pattern carefully and select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in it.

First row- 47, 52, 57

Second row- 69, 74, 79

Third row- 85, 91, ?
questions.solution:
Logic : (3rd number + 1st number) = (2 × 2nd number)

So,

__
 
• First row: 47, 52, 57

57 + 47 = 2 × 52

104 = 104 (LHS = RHS) 

And,

 
• Second row: 69, 74, 79

79 + 69 = 2 × 74

148 = 148 (LHS = RHS)

Similarly,

 
• Third row: 85, 91, ?

? + 85 = 2 × 91

? = **182 - 85**__

**? = 97**

Hence, "97" is the correct answer.

Five students Puneet, Karan, Chaman, Dinesh and Ronit having different ages study in same college. Ronit is elder than only Puneet and Karan. Dinesh is younger than only Chaman. Puneet is not the youngest. How many students are elder than Puneet?
questions.solution:
**Given :** Five students Puneet, Karan, Chaman, Dinesh and Ronit having different ages study in same college.

**Explanation : **

1) Dinesh is younger than only Chaman.

Chaman > Dinesh > _ > _ > _

2) Ronit is elder than only Puneet and Karan.

3) Puneet is not the youngest.

Chaman > Dinesh > Ronit > Puneet > Karan

Thus, according to the final arrangement three students are elder than Puneet i.e Chaman, Dinesh and Ronit.

Hence, **"3"** is the correct answer.
